newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds set to rise, bund yield gap to narrow.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds set to rise, bund yield gap to narrow.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose slightly at the opening of trade on Wednesday, following overnight Wall Street gains with dealers foreseeing a further narrowing of the Danish-German 10-year yield differential.
"Foreign investors showed solid interest in Danish bonds yesterday and this could well continue today," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened up 0.07 point from Tuesday's close at 113.76, yielding 5.92 percent, while the upcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark started off 0.12 point higher at 106.56, with yield at 6.11 percent.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged from noon yesterday at 57 basis points. The crown opened at an unaltered 3.8081 per mark.
